C1_GENERATION_TRANSACTION_AND_PUBLICATIO.summary: Candidate revision fencing, accepted-state bookkeeping, runtime-generation allocation, and publication are not treated as one serialized acceptance transaction.
architectural_invariants: Per-source stale, duplicate, and same-revision conflict decisions remain valid when rechecked under the single writer.
Rejected candidates do not advance accepted revision, runtime generation, serving state, or durable acceptance.
Exactly one complete immutable RuntimeSnapshot becomes visible atomically.

C2_STABLE_IDENTITY_AND_COMPATIBILITY.summary: Reconciliation uses unstable or insufficient identity and compatibility keys, confusing continuous membership with replacement and semantic equivalence with change.
architectural_invariants: Endpoint identity is canonical and duplicate canonical identities are rejected.
Continuously unchanged endpoints and compatible pools preserve runtime continuity.
Accepted removal followed by re-add creates a new endpoint incarnation.
Semantic digests are independent of declaration-only ordering.

C3_REQUEST_SNAPSHOT_AND_SELECTION_ELIGIB.summary: Request processing does not consistently bind selection, affinity, retry, and failover decisions to one leased generation plus current incarnation eligibility.
architectural_invariants: A request acquires one RuntimeSnapshot and retains it for its complete lifetime.
Sticky, retry, weighted, and failover selection use only members in that leased snapshot.
Every assignment rechecks membership incarnation, lifecycle, and health eligibility.
No eligible backend produces deterministic service-unavailable behavior.

C4_DRAIN_TRANSPORT_AND_RETIREMENT_OWNERS.summary: Removal, transport draining, reachability, and lifecycle-owned retirement are not coordinated as one ownership state machine.
architectural_invariants: Removed membership is ineligible for new work before publication of the new generation.
Existing traffic may finish until completion or the drain deadline.
Runtime objects remain alive while snapshots, in-flight work, or reusable transport references require them.
Lifecycle-scoped telemetry is released when its owner is finally retired.

C5_CHECKPOINT_COMMIT_AND_RECOVERY.summary: Durable checkpoint commit, acknowledgement, integrity verification, fallback, and reconstruction are not aligned with the published-generation acceptance boundary.
architectural_invariants: A complete checkpoint body is durable before CURRENT can reference it.
CURRENT becomes recoverable only after the corresponding complete runtime snapshot is published.
Acceptance is acknowledged only after CURRENT replacement and directory durability.
Recovery verifies integrity, falls back to a previous complete state, and recompiles a whole generation.
Only compatible, non-expired continuity state is restored.

C6_INGRESS_COALESCING_AND_SOURCE_AUTHORI.summary: Complete-snapshot ingestion does not preserve per-source revision authority and last-accepted source state under burst coalescing, rejection, and restart.
architectural_invariants: Each independent source has its own accepted revision fence and accepted complete snapshot.
Bounded queues may coalesce superseded complete snapshots but must converge to the newest admissible snapshot.
Rejected candidates cannot replace accepted source material used by later merges.
Recovered source-revision fences are installed before watchers or providers resume.

defects.observable_failure: A source revision already accepted with one content digest can later be treated as an idempotent duplicate or replacement when the same revision arrives with different content, so the conflict is not rejected deterministically.
defects.partial_fix_trap: Adding a duplicate-revision fast path is insufficient if it compares only the revision; the accepted digest and under-writer fence still have to participate in the decision.

defects.observable_failure: An older source revision that began validation before a newer revision was accepted can publish after the newer generation because the stale fence is not rechecked inside the serialized reconciliation writer.
defects.partial_fix_trap: Serializing only the final snapshot swap still permits a candidate validated against an obsolete accepted-revision set to win unless source fences are revalidated inside that serialization boundary.

defects.observable_failure: A candidate rejected during semantic validation or compilation can still advance accepted source-revision or runtime-generation bookkeeping, causing a later valid update to be rejected as stale or to skip a generation despite the serving snapshot remaining unchanged.
defects.partial_fix_trap: Preserving the old serving pointer alone does not fix poisoned acceptance metadata; all accepted-revision, generation, checkpoint, and status mutations must remain outside the rejected path.

defects.observable_failure: An exact duplicate source snapshot with the same accepted revision and digest still allocates a runtime generation and performs reconciliation, creating avoidable checkpoint, drain, and lifecycle churn instead of an idempotent no-op.
defects.partial_fix_trap: Suppressing only the public update notification leaves hidden generation allocation, metrics, checkpoint bodies, or drain transitions growing unless the duplicate is stopped before candidate reconciliation.

defects.observable_failure: A request can observe a new route graph together with old or not-yet-reconciled pool runtime state because publication exposes generation pieces separately instead of exchanging one complete RuntimeSnapshot.
defects.partial_fix_trap: Putting a lock around route replacement does not restore the invariant if pool views, runtime handles, or generation metadata are still installed through separate visibility points.

defects.observable_failure: Equivalent endpoint addresses that normalize to the same network identity are accepted as distinct members, splitting health, balancing, affinity, transport, and metric state for one backend.
defects.partial_fix_trap: Deduplicating raw address strings misses equivalent textual forms; canonicalization must precede uniqueness checks and the same canonical identity must be used throughout reconciliation and selection.

defects.observable_failure: A declaration reorder or equivalent address formatting change makes a continuously present endpoint look removed and re-added, resetting health and selection continuity and unnecessarily starting a drain.
defects.partial_fix_trap: Preserving health by copying values into the replacement object still loses incarnation, affinity, balancer, transport, and lifecycle continuity; the unchanged identity itself has to be stable.

defects.observable_failure: A material selection or affinity policy change is classified as runtime-compatible, so balancer or sticky state created under old semantics is silently reused by the new pool generation.
defects.partial_fix_trap: Resetting only sticky entries is incomplete when weighted-balancer continuity, counters, health aggregates, or endpoint references are also policy-sensitive; compatibility needs one coherent fingerprint.

defects.observable_failure: A semantically unchanged pool is classified as incompatible because declaration-only ordering or non-semantic metadata participates in its compatibility key, so unrelated reloads discard useful balancing and affinity continuity.
defects.partial_fix_trap: Ignoring one ordering field merely moves the instability if the compatibility identity is not defined from normalized semantic policy; a hand-picked copy of affinity state also leaves other reusable state reset.

defects.observable_failure: When an endpoint is absent from one accepted generation and then reappears, reconciliation reactivates its still-draining runtime object instead of creating a new membership incarnation.
defects.partial_fix_trap: Flipping the lifecycle flag back to ACTIVE makes selection appear fixed but carries the old drain deadline, in-flight accounting, transport ownership, health evidence, and metric scope into the new membership.

defects.observable_failure: A request or stream reacquires the current snapshot during a retry or later forwarding phase, allowing one request to resolve routes or pools from two different generations.
defects.partial_fix_trap: Caching only the initial route result is insufficient if retries, failover, affinity, or forwarding later consult the global current snapshot; the lease must cover the complete request lifetime.

defects.observable_failure: Sticky affinity can route to a target whose canonical identity still exists but whose membership incarnation is stale, draining, or unhealthy because affinity lookup does not revalidate full eligibility before use.
defects.partial_fix_trap: Deleting mappings only when an endpoint disappears misses remove/re-add incarnation changes and health transitions; every lookup must validate the current leased membership incarnation and health.

defects.observable_failure: A DRAINING endpoint remains eligible for new weighted selection because membership lifecycle is not checked independently of health.
defects.partial_fix_trap: Marking draining endpoints unhealthy couples two independent state machines and can corrupt preserved health evidence on reconfiguration; selection must enforce lifecycle eligibility directly.

defects.observable_failure: A retry can select the same failed canonical endpoint again after an alias, handle replacement, or reconciliation remap because the attempted set is keyed by an unstable runtime handle rather than stable endpoint identity.
defects.partial_fix_trap: Increasing the retry budget or excluding only the immediately previous pointer hides the loop for simple cases but does not provide request-local canonical endpoint exclusion across attempts.

defects.observable_failure: When every backend in the primary and configured failover pools is ineligible, selection still forwards to a known unhealthy or draining member instead of returning deterministic service-unavailable behavior.
defects.partial_fix_trap: Adding an all-unhealthy check only to the primary pool remains unsafe if failover traversal can choose ineligible members; eligibility has to gate every pool in the chain.

defects.observable_failure: Failover for a request leased to an older generation resolves the failover pool from the globally current registry, so a concurrent publication can change that request's failover target mid-flight.
defects.partial_fix_trap: Holding the route object stable does not help if failover pool resolution is global; route policy, pool chain, and membership views must all come from the same leased snapshot.

defects.observable_failure: A removed endpoint is not marked ineligible until after the next RuntimeSnapshot is published, leaving a transition window in which new requests can still be assigned to capacity that the accepted membership has removed.
defects.partial_fix_trap: Making the drain worker faster narrows but does not eliminate the unsafe window; the lifecycle transition must precede publication and selection must honor it.

defects.observable_failure: Removing an endpoint closes or discards its runtime and reusable transport state immediately, terminating or stranding in-flight and long-lived traffic that legitimately holds an older snapshot lease.
defects.partial_fix_trap: Keeping only the socket open is not enough if the endpoint runtime, in-flight counters, health reference, or old snapshot reachability is retired underneath the request.

defects.observable_failure: Drain completion ignores outstanding old-generation snapshot reachability and can retire an endpoint runtime while a leased request still holds a valid reference to that incarnation.
defects.partial_fix_trap: Waiting for the in-flight counter alone fails for streams or reusable transport references not represented by that counter; retirement needs the complete ownership/reachability condition.

defects.observable_failure: Idle reusable connections or post-removal keepalive reuse can keep a drain alive indefinitely or permit fresh work onto a draining endpoint, so configured drain deadlines do not bound retirement.
defects.partial_fix_trap: Adding a timer that only flips the endpoint to RETIRED leaves reusable connections and assignment paths alive; deadline handling must coordinate transport retirement and no-new-work semantics.

defects.observable_failure: Retired endpoint incarnations or unreachable generations leave lifecycle-scoped metric registrations behind, so repeated membership and generation turnover produces stale observations and unbounded metric cardinality.
defects.partial_fix_trap: Deleting metric values on removal is either too early for live old snapshots or too late for stuck scopes; metric ownership must follow final endpoint and generation reachability rather than configuration presence alone.

defects.observable_failure: The recoverable CURRENT pointer can reference a generation before its complete checkpoint body is durably fsynced or before the corresponding complete RuntimeSnapshot has been published, allowing restart to select a partial or never-safely-published generation.
defects.partial_fix_trap: Atomic rename of CURRENT by itself is not sufficient; body durability and publication ordering must precede the pointer commit, and directory durability must complete the transaction.

defects.observable_failure: An update can be acknowledged as accepted after in-memory publication but before the CURRENT pointer replacement and state-directory fsync are durable, so a crash can lose a generation the operator was told was accepted.
defects.partial_fix_trap: Writing the checkpoint body earlier does not give accepted semantics if recovery authority still points to the previous generation; acknowledgement must wait for the durable pointer commit.

defects.observable_failure: Startup can trust a corrupt, truncated, checksum-mismatched, or schema-incompatible CURRENT checkpoint and become ready with incomplete desired state instead of rejecting that recovery point.
defects.partial_fix_trap: Checking that the file parses is insufficient; pointer metadata, schema, checksum, generation metadata, and complete normalized desired state all have to be validated before compilation/publication.

defects.observable_failure: A corrupt or incomplete CURRENT checkpoint causes startup failure even when a retained previous complete checkpoint or configured bootstrap state is valid, turning recoverable corruption into unnecessary unavailability.
defects.partial_fix_trap: Catching the CURRENT read error without an ordered complete-state fallback still leaves the process not-ready; fallback must preserve the same integrity and whole-generation validation rules.

defects.observable_failure: Recovery republishes serialized runtime objects or continuity state without fully revalidating and recompiling normalized desired state, allowing incompatible policy state or expired/stale affinity and health continuity to survive restart.
defects.partial_fix_trap: Revalidating only configuration syntax leaves runtime compatibility and expiry unchecked; recovery must rebuild the whole generation and selectively restore only compatible, non-expired continuity state.

defects.observable_failure: Under a burst that fills the bounded ingress queue, coalescing can discard the newest complete snapshot and retain a superseded one, so the runtime converges to stale endpoint membership after the burst quiets.
defects.partial_fix_trap: Increasing queue capacity only delays the failure; coalescing must understand complete-snapshot replacement and retain the newest admissible revision per source.

defects.observable_failure: Revision ordering is tracked globally across independent configuration or discovery sources, so a high revision from one source can cause a valid lower-numbered revision from another source to be rejected as stale.
defects.partial_fix_trap: Namespacing only the input queue is incomplete if accepted-revision bookkeeping or reconciliation fences remain global; source identity must scope revision authority end to end.

defects.observable_failure: A source snapshot that is later rejected can still replace the cached accepted snapshot used for multi-source merging, so an unrelated valid update from another source is compiled against rejected desired state.
defects.partial_fix_trap: Keeping the serving RuntimeSnapshot unchanged does not protect future candidates if the ingress merge cache was mutated; accepted source material must advance only with successful acceptance.

defects.observable_failure: After restart, watchers or discovery providers can resume before recovered per-source revision fences are installed, allowing an older complete snapshot to roll the recovered desired state backward.
defects.partial_fix_trap: Starting providers later by a fixed delay is racy; recovered accepted revisions must become authoritative before update admission is enabled.

normal: Initial valid desired state is normalized, compiled, checkpoint-prepared, atomically published, durably accepted, and serves requests through healthy eligible backends.
A route-only semantic change publishes a new generation while compatible unchanged pool and endpoint runtime state remains reusable.
A membership addition creates only the new endpoint runtime state while continuously unchanged members retain health, balancing, affinity, and transport continuity.
An exact duplicate accepted source revision and digest is an idempotent no-op with no serving-generation, drain, checkpoint, or lifecycle-scope churn.
Independent complete-snapshot sources merge using their own revision authorities and the last accepted snapshot from every other source.
A long-lived request keeps its original generation lease across an unrelated publication and completes against a coherent route/pool view.
Restart from a complete accepted checkpoint reconstructs one complete generation and resumes update admission with recovered source-revision fences already authoritative.
edge_boundary: Equivalent endpoint address spellings and declaration reordering preserve canonical identity and semantic equivalence while duplicate canonical identities remain distinguishable as invalid input.
The boundary between same-revision/same-digest idempotency and same-revision/different-digest conflict is deterministic under concurrent arrivals.
An endpoint that is absent for exactly one accepted generation and then reappears is a new incarnation even while the old incarnation may still be draining.
Drain completion at the configured deadline accounts for in-flight work, reusable connections, and old-snapshot reachability without permitting new assignment.
Pool compatibility distinguishes semantic policy changes from declaration-only or metadata-only changes so reusable runtime state is neither over-reused nor needlessly reset.
Burst ingestion at queue capacity converges to the newest admissible complete snapshot for each source rather than an intermediate superseded state.
A health transition that leaves every primary and failover member ineligible reaches the explicit no-eligible-backend boundary rather than selecting a known-ineligible member.
negative_rejection: Semantically invalid configuration, missing references, invalid policy bounds, or duplicate canonical endpoint identities are rejected without advancing accepted source state or changing the serving generation.
An out-of-order source revision is rejected even if its validation began before a newer revision was accepted.
A repeated accepted source revision with different content is rejected as a conflict and cannot replace the accepted desired snapshot.
A sticky mapping to an unhealthy, draining, retired, or different-incarnation target is invalidated before selection.
Retries exclude already attempted canonical endpoints and never convert a retry budget into repeated attempts against the same failing target.
If neither the selected pool nor its configured failover chain has an eligible member, forwarding fails deterministically instead of routing to known-ineligible capacity.
A material selection or affinity policy incompatibility prevents reuse of runtime state created under the old semantics.
failure_recovery: A crash before runtime publication leaves the previous complete durable generation authoritative.
A crash after publication but before durable CURRENT commit may discard the unacknowledged generation on restart but cannot make it durably accepted.
A crash after CURRENT replacement and directory durability recovers the newly accepted complete generation.
Corrupt or incomplete CURRENT state is rejected and recovery attempts the retained previous complete generation before bootstrap or not-ready fallback.
With no complete valid checkpoint or bootstrap source, startup remains not-ready and never publishes partial desired state.
Recovery recompiles normalized desired state and restores only compatible non-expired continuity data before one atomic publication.
A backend removed during an active request stops receiving new assignments while traffic already holding valid ownership may finish within drain policy.
cross_component: A combined route, pool, and endpoint update crosses validation, compilation, reconciliation, checkpoint preparation, lifecycle transitions, and one publication boundary without exposing a mixed generation.
Rapid remove/re-add keeps the old draining incarnation, transport accounting, health evidence, and metric scope separate from the newly active incarnation.
Passive health feedback racing an unrelated configuration publication remains attached to the compatible endpoint runtime object and affects eligibility without mutating configuration generations.
A duplicate or rejected update cannot indirectly create drains, checkpoint authority changes, runtime-generation scopes, or stale metrics.
Generation and endpoint telemetry is retained while its owning live snapshot or endpoint incarnation remains reachable and is released only after final lifecycle retirement.
A rejected snapshot from one source cannot contaminate the accepted merge base used when another source later submits a valid snapshot.

A request using failover after a concurrent publication follows the failover chain and membership views from its own leased generation, while lifecycle and health eligibility are checked against owned runtime state.
Recovered checkpoint authority, recovered source fences, and resumed ingress cooperate so provider replay cannot roll back the restored serving generation.
